In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
no single biomarker has emerged to date as the ideal diagnostic or prognostic tool for prostate cancer.
no single molecular signature can be used to accurately distinguish indolent prostate cancer from aggressive prostate cancer.
the identification of a panel of prognostic biomarker(s) in blood and/or urine is still in its infancy, but the future of this field is bright.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we identified novel biomarkers in serum and urine that may have potential to be used in the clinical management of prostate cancer.
the identification of a panel of biomarkers for the diagnosis of prostate cancer and the risk of progression to aggressive disease is an active and exciting area of investigation.
we are still far from the ideal biomarkers that can accurately distinguish between indolent and aggressive prostate tumors.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the identification of biomarker panels that can accurately predict the clinical outcome of prostate cancer patients is feasible and will be achieved in the near future.
the development of robust, noninvasive diagnostic tests for the early detection of prostate cancer will require the use of a panel of biomarkers.
the use of novel technologies and the application of innovative approaches are required to identify the best candidates for biomarker discovery.
